subtype: Approach: mock tests then error analysis [Action]
passage: Drilling from the flat above went on all Saturday morning, but Vasudha finished the full mock paper anyway, earplugs and all. By evening she had marked it and copied every wrong answer onto a sheet with three headings: concept gap, careless slip, ran out of time. Kamal, her elder brother, tallied at the door. Twelve concept gaps, nine careless slips, ten time-pressure. “Concept, then?” he asked. “Concept. Rotation and thermodynamics.” She built next week around those two: three sessions on rotation, two on thermodynamics and one short timed set for speed. The careless slips she pinned to the fridge on a note that read check the sign.

qa.q: How many concept gaps did Vasudha find?
What might Vasudha be feeling as she plans the week around rotation and thermodynamics?
qa.a: Focused and a little relieved: sorting the mistakes turned a vague sense of failing into a clear task.

qa.q: What else could Vasudha do about the careless slips, and why?
qa.a: Use a fixed two-minute checking routine at the end of each section, since it targets that kind of slip directly.

qa.q: How does the plan look to Kamal?
qa.a: Kamal, who tallied the mistakes, sees a younger sister choosing the biggest problem instead of trying to fix everything, and may offer to quiz her.

grounding: A teen takes a full mock weekly, sorts mistakes into concept, careless and time categories, and plans around the largest.
